regime_classification.growth: {"dimension":"growth","metric_summary":"GDP 7.8%; PMI 54.6","signal_text":"GDP at 7.8% is the headline; GVA at approximately 6.1% is the reality, with the 170bps gap explained by statistical discrepancy rather than output. PMI composite at 54.6 (83rd percentile) is supported by services at 54.5 — but manufacturing PMI slipped to 52.8 from 53.5, and IIP overall decelerated to 6.7% from 8.8%. The quality question: capacity utilisation at 77.4% is rising, which is genuine — but core sector at 5.4% and falling suggests the investment impulse is narrower than the headline implies.","badge_label":"Slowing Pace","badge_type":"b-slow"}
regime_classification.inflation: {"dimension":"inflation","metric_summary":"CPI 4.45%; Fuel 22.93%","signal_text":"CPI at 4.45% is above the 4% midpoint, but the real alarm is the composition: fuel inflation at 22.93% (95th percentile) is doing the heavy lifting, while core CPI at 3.9% (28th percentile) remains relatively contained. The inversion: a contained core would normally give RBI room to cut — but fuel at 22.93% feeds into WPI at 9.92%, which feeds into producer margins, which feeds into services prices with a two-quarter lag. RBI's own inflation forecast just jumped 50bps to 5.1%; the repo at 5.25% leaves a real rate of 15bps — insufficient to anchor expectations if fuel stays elevated.","badge_label":"Inflation Overshoot","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.credit: {"dimension":"credit","metric_summary":"Credit 17.1%; CD 81.4%","signal_text":"Bank credit at 17.1% YoY against deposit growth of 10.8% — a 630bps divergence — is the structural fault line. CD ratio at 81.4% has eased one month from 82.5% but remains at the 75th percentile; the prior cycle peak above 80% in FY14 preceded emergency rate hikes within 12 months. NBFC credit growth accelerating to 14.9% from 10.6% signals wholesale funding pressure building at the margin — NBFCs cannot mobilise retail deposits and are increasingly dependent on bank lines and bond markets at a time when both are tightening at the margin.","badge_label":"Deposit Gap Stress","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.policy: {"dimension":"policy","metric_summary":"Repo 5.25%","signal_text":"Repo at 5.25% (38th percentile) is historically accommodative, but the real rate at 15bps against a 91st-percentile INR and 95th-percentile fuel inflation is a policy contradiction. RBI cannot cut without risking INR depreciation and imported inflation; it cannot hike without stalling a capex cycle that is only 18 months old. The second-order effect of inaction: housing affordability improves as average home loan rates fall to 7.55%, but the INR at 96.15 means any external shock reprices the entire rate path overnight.","badge_label":"Rate Pause","badge_type":"b-neu"}
regime_classification.capex: {"dimension":"capex","metric_summary":"IIP CapG 16.1%; CU 77.4%","signal_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.1% and capacity utilisation at 77.4% — up from 75.6% — are the two numbers that justify optimism on private capex. The threshold that matters: private capex historically accelerates when utilisation crosses 78-80%; at 77.4%, India is one quarter away from that trigger. The contradiction is core sector at 5.4% and falling — cement and steel dispatch, the ground-level proxies for actual construction, are moderating even as the survey data looks firm. Order books in auto and steel are solid; execution is the variable.","badge_label":"Capex Upcycle","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.consumption: {"dimension":"consumption","metric_summary":"GST 199853; PV 16%","signal_text":"GST at ₹1,99,853 crore is a strong print, but the YTD at ₹10.42 lakh crore sits at only the 14th percentile — suggesting the monthly beat is partly seasonal and partly advance filing effects rather than a clean demand signal. The vehicle data is unambiguous: PV sales at 16%, two-wheelers at 19.7%, and CVs at 16.88% — all three segments firing simultaneously, which last happened in FY22's post-COVID rebound. The divergence to watch: two-wheeler strength at 19.7% signals rural income recovery, but airline passenger volumes at 86.4 million (35th percentile) suggest urban discretionary is not yet at cycle highs.","badge_label":"Demand Surge","badge_type":"b-exp"}

signal_cards.1: {"signal_num":1,"signal_theme":"CREDIT CYCLE","status":"risk","title":"Deposit Gap Forces RBI's Hand","data_text":"Bank credit growth at 17.1% YoY (Mar 2026) vs deposit growth at 10.8% — a 350bps divergence widening for three consecutive months. CD ratio at 81.4% (down from 82.5% prior month but structurally elevated at 75th percentile). NBFC credit growth accelerating to 14.9% YoY from 10.6%, signalling wholesale funding pressure. Credit-to-deposit gap now at its widest in the current cycle.","implication":"Banks with CASA ratios below 40% face deposit poaching risk; overweight private banks with CASA > 45% and strong digital franchises. Avoid NBFCs with wholesale funding > 30% of liabilities — they will face margin compression and refinancing risk if RBI tightens liquidity. Expect RBI to signal deposit-friendly measures (higher savings rates, CRR cuts) within 2-3 months. Underweight PSU banks with weak deposit franchises.","pct_10y":75,"pct_note":"CD ratio at 75th percentile historically preceded either RBI rate cuts (to ease deposit pressure) or sharp NBFC credit slowdowns. Last time CD ratio was this wide (2022), RBI cut rates 250bps within 6 months.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.2: {"signal_num":2,"signal_theme":"CAPEX TRIGGER","status":"positive","title":"Capacity Utilisation Signals Sustained Investment","data_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.1% YoY with capacity utilisation at 77.4% (up from 75.6% prior month, 74th percentile). Manufacturing PMI at 52.8 (down from 53.5 but still expansionary). Core sector growth at 5.4% YoY (down from 6.0%) — a moderation but not a collapse. Order books remain firm across auto, cement, and steel.","implication":"Capex cycle is self-sustaining; corporates are investing to fill capacity gaps, not speculating. Overweight capital goods manufacturers (Cummins, Timken, Bharat Electronics), cement (Ultratech, Ambuja), and industrial automation plays. Expect 18-24 month runway of sustained capex before capacity utilisation peaks above 80%. Avoid cyclical plays betting on demand surge — this is supply-side investment, not demand-driven.","pct_10y":74,"pct_note":"Capacity utilisation at 77.4% is at the 74th percentile; historically, sustained capex cycles begin when CU crosses 75% and continue until it reaches 82-85%. Current trajectory suggests 12-18 months of above-trend capex growth.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.3: {"signal_num":3,"signal_theme":"SIP / RETAIL FLOWS","status":"positive","title":"SIP AUM Surge Signals Affluent Money Entry","data_text":"SIP inflows at ₹32,297 Cr (up from ₹31,961 Cr, rising 2 consecutive months). SIP accounts at 100.18 Cr (up from 99.06 Cr). But SIP AUM at ₹18.62 Tr (up from ₹18.21 Tr, rising 2 consecutive months) — growing 40% faster than account growth. Average SIP AUM per account now ₹1.86 Lakh, up from ₹1.84 Lakh. MF AUM at ₹87.08 Tr (92nd percentile, rising 2 consecutive months). DII equity net at ₹58,502 Cr (100th percentile, rising 2 consecutive months).","implication":"Retail SIP base is maturing; average ticket size rising means affluent households (HNI/UHNI) are entering SIP, not mass retail. This is late-cycle behaviour — wealth concentration in equity markets. Overweight large-cap quality (Nifty 50 constituents with 20%+ ROE) and avoid micro/small-cap momentum plays. Expect SIP growth to decelerate as base effects kick in, but AUM growth will remain strong due to market appreciation and ticket size expansion. Position for a 12-18 month equity bull run, but hedge tail risk with long-dated puts.","pct_10y":92,"pct_note":"SIP AUM at 93rd percentile; historically, when SIP AUM growth outpaces account growth by >30%, equity markets have peaked within 6-12 months. Current divergence is the widest since 2021.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.4: {"signal_num":4,"signal_theme":"OIL / COMMODITY RISK","status":"risk","title":"Fuel Inflation Spike Threatens Margin Compression","data_text":"Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (up from 20.05%, 95th percentile). WPI at 9.92% (up from 9.78%, 67th percentile). Brent crude at $97.78/bbl (69th percentile, flat). Natural gas at $3.19/MMBtu (20th percentile, up from $2.88 — a 10% spike in 2 months). Iron ore at $161.91/tonne (up from $97.24, 63rd percentile). Copper at $6.76/lb (81st percentile, up 3 of last 5 months).","implication":"Fuel inflation is the primary driver of WPI overshoot; pass-through to CPI will accelerate in Q2 FY27. Avoid airlines (SpiceJet, IndiGo margin compression), logistics (Allcargo, TCI Express), and power generation (thermal coal exposure). Overweight refiners (Reliance, Hindustan Petroleum) with hedged crude exposure and downstream margin lock-in. Expect RBI to tolerate 5.0-5.2% CPI for 2-3 months before signalling rate cuts. Commodity-linked inflation is structural, not transitory.","pct_10y":95,"pct_note":"Fuel inflation at 95th percentile is the highest in the current cycle; last time fuel inflation spiked this high (2022), CPI overshot 6.5% and RBI hiked rates 250bps. Current RBI is more dovish, but margin compression in transport/logistics is inevitable.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.5: {"signal_num":5,"signal_theme":"GLOBAL LIQUIDITY","status":"watch","title":"BOJ Tightening Unwinds Carry Trade Slowly","data_text":"BOJ rate at 1.0% (up from 0.75%, 86th percentile, strong-negative signal). Fed funds at 3.63% (flat, 67th percentile). ECB deposit rate at 2.25% (up from 2.0%, 59th percentile). US 10Y Treasury at 4.96% (90th percentile, flat). DXY at 101.18 (53rd percentile, up 4 of last 5 months). US PMI composite at 56.0 (84th percentile, up from 54.5). Global PMI composite at 53.5 (82nd percentile). FII equity net at ₹29,631 Cr (83rd percentile, up 1 of last 2 months).","implication":"BOJ tightening is the tail risk; carry trades funded in JPY are unwinding slowly, not catastrophically. FII flows remain positive, suggesting global liquidity is still abundant. Monitor JPY strength (currently stable) and VIX (at 10.35, 5th percentile — complacency risk). If BOJ signals further hikes or JPY breaks above 95 (from current 96.15 INR/USD), expect sharp FII outflows and INR weakness. For now, maintain long equity exposure but hedge with long-dated OTM puts. US rates are sticky at 4.9-5.0% — no near-term Fed cuts expected.","pct_10y":86,"pct_note":"BOJ rate at 86th percentile is the highest in the current cycle; historically, BOJ tightening has preceded EM currency weakness and equity volatility spikes within 3-6 months. Current FII inflows suggest global investors are not yet pricing this risk.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.6: {"signal_num":6,"signal_theme":"INR / FX RESERVES","status":"risk","title":"INR Weakness Accelerates Despite RBI Intervention","data_text":"INR/USD at 96.15 (up from 95.73, 91st percentile, strong-negative signal). INR has weakened 90 paise in 5 months (95.24 → 96.15). India VIX at 10.35 (5th percentile, falling 5 consecutive months — complacency). US 10Y Treasury at 4.96% (90th percentile) vs RBI repo at 5.25% (38th percentile) — carry trade incentive is weakening. FII equity net at ₹29,631 Cr (positive) but FII debt flows are likely negative (not disclosed). Brent crude at $97.78 (69th percentile) — import bill pressure.","implication":"INR weakness is structural, not cyclical. RBI is intervening (evident from flat DXY despite INR weakness), but reserves are being deployed. If INR breaks 97.0, expect RBI to signal rate hikes or tighter liquidity. Overweight INR hedges (long USD calls, short INR forwards) for 6-12 month horizon. Avoid import-heavy sectors (pharma, auto components) unless they have strong USD revenue. Expect INR to trade 96.5-97.5 for next 2-3 months before stabilising. FII equity inflows are masking debt outflows — watch for reversal.","pct_10y":91,"pct_note":"INR weakness at 91st percentile is the highest in the current cycle; historically, when INR weakens this sharply, RBI has either hiked rates or tightened liquidity within 2-3 months. Current RBI is data-dependent but will act if INR breaks 97.0.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.7: {"signal_num":7,"signal_theme":"UNDER THE RADAR","status":"surprise","title":"Retail Mall Vacancy Collapse Signals GCC Absorption","data_text":"Retail mall vacancy at 5.0% (down from 7.5%, 8th percentile, strong-positive signal). Office absorption at 26.9 Mn sqft (down from 24.1 Mn sqft, 21st percentile, mild-negative signal). Office vacancy at 14.5% (down from 16.1%, 42nd percentile). Nifty IT index flat YTD despite office absorption remaining firm. But retail mall vacancy has collapsed to 8th percentile — the lowest in the current cycle. This divergence is non-obvious: office RE is decoupling from IT services (GCCs are the buyer, not traditional IT), while retail RE is being absorbed by non-traditional tenants (quick commerce, D2C, cloud kitchens).","implication":"Retail mall REITs (Embassy, Mindspace, Brookfield) are undervalued. Retail mall vacancy at 5% signals pricing power and rental growth acceleration. Quick commerce (Blinkit, Zepto, Dunzo) and cloud kitchen operators (Rebel Foods, Faasos) are the new anchor tenants, not traditional retail. Overweight retail mall REITs for 12-18 month horizon; expect 8-12% rental growth and 200-300bps cap rate compression. Avoid office REITs betting on IT services recovery — GCC absorption is structural, not cyclical. This is a 2-3 year structural shift in commercial RE demand patterns.","pct_10y":8,"pct_note":"Retail mall vacancy at 8th percentile is the lowest in the current cycle; historically, when retail vacancy falls below 10%, rental growth accelerates 300-500bps and REIT valuations re-rate upward by 15-25% within 12 months. Last time retail vacancy was this tight (2019), retail REITs outperformed office REITs by 800bps.","is_surprise":true}

executive_summary.1:
{"para_num":1,"para_label":"India Macro Regime","para_html":"

Consumption Fires on All Cylinders — Margins Pay the Price

The facts:

  • PV, two-wheeler, and CV sales all grew 16–20% YoY simultaneously — a broad-based demand signal last seen in FY22.
  • GST at ₹1,99,853 Cr looks like a record; but YTD at ₹10.42 lakh crore sits at the 14th percentile — advance filings flatter the monthly print.
  • Fuel inflation at 22.93% (95th percentile) feeds into WPI at 9.92% — producer cost pressure that services CPI will absorb within two quarters.
  • But core CPI at 3.9% (28th percentile) remains contained, creating a false sense of comfort at the headline level.

The tension: Demand is real — three vehicle segments and retail mall vacancy at a cycle-low 5% confirm it. But fuel at 22.93% is a margin tax on every business serving that demand; the consumer is present, the producer's profitability is not.

Bottom line: Watch two-wheeler sales as the rural income proxy — a deceleration below 15% would signal the consumption story is narrowing to urban affluent only.

"}
executive_summary.2:
{"para_num":2,"para_label":"Global Macro Regime","para_html":"

DM Surveys Accelerate — Nominal GDP Says Otherwise

The facts:

  • US PMI composite at 56.0 (84th percentile) and Global PMI at 53.5 (82nd percentile) signal re-acceleration.
  • But US GDP SAAR slowed to 1.5% from 2.1%, and China GDP fell to 4.3% from 5.0% with PMI at 49.5 — contraction territory.
  • US 10Y at 4.96% (90th percentile) is doing the Fed's tightening for it; real economy stress is already embedded in the yield curve.
  • BOJ at 1.0% (86th percentile, up from 0.75%) is the underappreciated variable — yen carry unwind accelerates as the rate differential compresses.

The tension: Survey data prices re-acceleration; nominal GDP data prices deceleration. China at 4.3% prevents commodity reflation from sustaining, which is the one scenario that would validate the survey optimism.

Bottom line: BOJ's next move is the tail risk for India liquidity — a further 25bps hike would accelerate FII repatriation from EM into yen-denominated assets.

"}
executive_summary.3:
{"para_num":3,"para_label":"Liquidity Conditions","para_html":"

Domestic Flows at Record Highs — Funded by Thinner Deposit Base

The facts:

  • DII equity net at ₹58,502 Cr (100th percentile, rising two consecutive months) — domestic capital is absorbing every FII wobble.
  • SIP AUM at ₹18.62 Tr growing 40% faster than account growth — average ticket size rising to ₹1.86 lakh signals affluent money deepening, not mass participation widening.
  • But bank deposit growth at 10.8% vs credit at 17.1% — the same pool funding SIP inflows is being stretched to fund loan books simultaneously.
  • FII equity net at ₹29,631 Cr (83rd percentile) is positive, but FII debt flows are likely negative given INR at 96.15 and US 10Y at 4.96%.

The tension: Equity liquidity looks abundant; the underlying deposit base funding both credit growth and mutual fund inflows is not. SIP inflows are a flow, not a stock — a sentiment shift in the affluent segment reverses them faster than CASA deposits.

Bottom line: If SIP YoY growth (currently 14%, down from 16%) falls below 10%, DII absorption capacity shrinks and the market loses its domestic bid.

"}
executive_summary.4:
{"para_num":4,"para_label":"Equity + Real Estate Implications","para_html":"

Retail Real Estate Tightens — Listed REITs Disagree Loudly

The facts:

  • Retail mall vacancy collapsed to 5.0% (8th percentile, down from 7.5%) — the tightest in the current cycle, driven by quick commerce, D2C, and cloud kitchen tenants.
  • Office absorption at 26.9 Mn sqft (21st percentile) is GCC-led, not traditional IT — Nifty IT flat YTD is the wrong lens for office RE.
  • But Embassy, Mindspace, and Brookfield REITs are down 15–25% YTD — listed proxies pricing a vacancy story the physical market has already resolved.
  • Nifty 50 at 23,447 (75th percentile) and Bank Nifty at 56,549 (93rd percentile) — banking index at near-cycle highs while deposit stress is structurally unresolved.

The tension: Physical real estate — both retail and office — is tightening. Listed REITs are pricing distress. Bank Nifty at 93rd percentile assumes NIM stability that a 630bps credit-deposit divergence will eventually challenge.

Bottom line: REITs at 15–25% discounts to physical market fundamentals are a mispricing worth monitoring — but the catalyst requires FII debt flows to stabilise, which needs INR below 95.

"}
executive_summary.5:
{"para_num":5,"para_label":"Key Risks to Monitor","para_html":"

Four Fuses, One Detonator — INR Holds Them All Together

The facts:

  • INR at 96.15 (91st percentile, weakened 90 paise in 5 months) — every further leg down reprices import costs, fuel subsidies, and FII return calculations simultaneously.
  • Fuel inflation at 22.93% (95th percentile) — if Brent sustains above $100, the pass-through to CPI forces RBI's hand on rates regardless of growth signals.
  • CD ratio at 81.4% (75th percentile) with NBFC credit accelerating to 14.9% — the last time this ratio sustained above 80% with a thin real rate, macro-prudential tightening followed within three quarters.
  • India VIX at 10.35 (5th percentile, falling five consecutive months) — complacency at this level historically precedes a volatility spike of 40–60% within 60 days.

The tension: Each risk is manageable in isolation; INR weakness is the transmission mechanism that makes them simultaneous — a depreciating rupee tightens imported inflation, pressures RBI, raises NBFC funding costs, and triggers FII outflows in one chain.

Bottom line: Watch INR/USD — a print above 97.00 this week would force RBI intervention that drains liquidity and reprices the entire rate-cut narrative the equity market is still holding.

"}
